subject: Deferring Admission Offers

Please be aware that candidates who reactivate their applications are essentially reapplying for admission. Applicants who were not previously admitted cannot use the reactivation application process to apply again.

The Columbia Engineering School has a strict policy in regards to applying to only one program within the school. Since our MS programs (MSOR, MSIE, MSBA, MS&E, MSFE) are all in the Engineering School, you may only apply to one of our MS programs per cycle.

While there are no official prerequisites for our programs, we do ask that our students have a background in multivariable calculus, linear algebra, and probability & statistics. It would also help if you have some knowledge of computer languages C++, Python, and Matlab. Overall, we place the highest priority on quantitative skills, followed by programming experience, and internship/work experience.

subject: Prerequisites for Graduate Programs
utterances: Are there prerequisites for your programs?
What courses do I need before applying?
What background is required for the MS programs?
response_template:
Hello {student_name},

There are no official mandatory prerequisites for our programs. However, we do ask that our students have a background in multivariable calculus, linear algebra, and probability & statistics. It would also help if you have some knowledge of computer languages C++, Python, and Matlab. We place the highest priority on quantitative skills, followed by math grades, programming experience, and internship/work experience.

For our MSOR & MSIE programs, we highly recommend that students have completed:
• 1 course on multivariate calculus
• 1 course on linear algebra
• 1 additional math course (e.g., differential equations, discrete math, real analysis)
• 1 course on probability (or a joint course in probability and statistics)

Programming experience is preferred and admitted students without sufficient experience will be required to take a programming-based course.

Best regards,
Academic Advising Team

subject: What Makes the MSBA Program Special
utterances: What makes the Columbia MS in Business Analytics program special?
Tell me about the MSBA program.
Why should I choose the MSBA?
response_template:
Hello {student_name},

The Columbia MSBA program is a graduate program offered in partnership between Columbia Engineering and Columbia Business Schools. This practitioner-oriented professional MS program is led by faculty from three world-renowned areas: the IEOR Department, the Columbia Business Marketing Division, and the Columbia Business Decision Risk and Operations Division.

From a curriculum perspective, the MSBA program focuses on real-world applications to various industries, grounded by a rigorous foundation in Engineering and Business. Business Analytics is about using data science tools for solving operational and marketing problems. Students learn the data science tools and use them in conjunction with models to make better business decisions. Students are also engaged in a year-long capstone projects course, where they consult and collaborate with key industry partners.

Best regards,
Academic Advising Team

subject: What Makes the MS&E Program Special
utterances: What makes the Columbia MS in Management Sciences and Engineering program special?
Tell me about the MS&E program.
What is the Operations Consulting Course?
response_template:
Hello {student_name},

The Operations Consulting Course is what sets the MS&E program apart from other programs. This is a year-long course (2 semesters: fall and spring) where you work with a team of students on a scope of work with one of our partnering employers. The projects span a variety of industries including luxury goods, pharmaceuticals, finance, tourism, start-ups, consulting, and more. These are real companies, mostly regional but some global.

This course enables you to apply what you are learning from your coursework in a real-world way. You earn credits for this course, and many times partnering companies hire students for summer internships and full-time opportunities, though this is not a requirement.

Best regards,
Academic Advising Team

Academic Advising Team

subject: Adding Materials After Application Submission
utterances: Can I add new materials after submitting my application?
I want to add something to my application after I submitted it.
How do I upload supplemental materials?
response_template:
Hello {student_name},

If you have new or additional materials you would like to include with your application, you may upload them as a "Supplemental Material" in your Status Portal. Examples of supplemental materials include awards, certificates, school papers, etc. If you would like to provide updated or new test scores, please use the Updated Test Score form — this form should only be used if you have received new scores since submitting your application.

Best regards,
Academic Advising Team

subject: How Long MS Programs Take to Complete
utterances: How long does it take to complete the MS program?
How many semesters is the MS program?
Can I finish the MS in two semesters?
response_template:
Hello {student_name},

Students typically complete our programs in 3 semesters. Our MSBA, MSFE, and MS&E programs are 36 points. For our 30-point MS programs in Operations Research and Industrial Engineering, students can complete the program in 2 semesters by taking 15 points (usually 5 courses) per semester.

Best regards,
Academic Advising Team

subject: Graduate Program Class Profile
utterances: What is the class profile?

What type of students do you look for?
response_template:
Hello {student_name},

The Columbia IEOR graduate programs look for candidates with a background in engineering, mathematics, computer science, statistics, economics, finance, or other similar quantitative fields.

Best regards,
Academic Advising Team

subject: Expired Test Scores
utterances: Can I submit expired test scores?
My test scores have expired.
Will you accept scores that are no longer valid?
response_template:
Hello {student_name},

Expired test scores are not accepted. All standardized test scores need to remain valid through the start of your first semester. If your scores will expire prior to this, we strongly encourage you to retake the exam.

Best regards,
Academic Advising Team

subject: Application Interview Process
utterances: Is there an interview process?
Will I need to do an interview?
What does the video interview involve?
response_template:
Hello {student_name},

After submitting the application, applicants will have access to submit a video interview in the application portal. You will be asked 3 random questions and will have 3 minutes to answer. Please answer as if we were having a face-to-face conversation. There's no need to stress — it's just a way for us to get to know you better. Please submit your interview by the deadline listed in your interview link email.

Best regards,
Academic Advising Team

subject: Minimum GPA for Graduate Admission
utterances: Is there a minimum GPA for application?

What is the GPA requirement for admission?
response_template:

Yes, a 3.0 (out of 4) GPA is preferred. Most successful applicants have a GPA higher than 3.0.

Best regards,
Academic Advising Team

subject: When Admission Decisions Are Released
utterances: When will I know the decision?

How long does it take to get an admissions decision?
response_template:
Hello {student_name},

Applicants to the MS programs (Financial Engineering, Management Science & Engineering, Industrial Engineering, and Operations Research) for the Fall semester will be notified of their admissions decision or contacted for more information from mid-March to late-April. The IEOR Department does not have rolling admissions. Applications are reviewed after the priority deadline and the review process typically requires 6–10 weeks.

Best regards,
Academic Advising Team

Career placement and career development opportunities are offered by the IEOR Department, the Professional Development & Leadership team, and the Graduate Career Placement team. subject: CA Eligibility After Graduation

response_template:
Hello {student_name},

No, CA positions are only for currently enrolled students. You must be a current student the semester that you are working as a CA. In addition, if you complete all of your classes before the semester ends, your CA eligibility will also end by that date. You cannot be a CA if you are no longer attending in-person classes.

Academic Advising Team
